customer-jane: Hi, we rotated an API key this morning and since ~09:12 UTC a subset of requests from our web app are getting 401 invalid_api_key. Only affects users on Chrome with the PWA installed (service worker enabled). No errors for users without the PWA.

mia-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you share a minimal repro (curl or fetch) and whether you're hitting the hosted Redwood API or a Dedicated endpoint? Also the error body you see.

customer-jane: We're on hosted. Error body: {"error":"invalid_api_key", "message":"invalid key"}. Minimal repro is simple fetch from the PWA: 
```js
fetch('https://api.redwood.run/v1/chat', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer REPLACED_KEY', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood/rlhf-v1', input: 'hi' })
})
```
We rotate keys using our dashboard export and update env in our front-end build pipeline. The PWA still uses the old key somehow.

mia-support: Thanks — two quick checks: 1) can you confirm the last 6 chars of the active key vs the one failing (we don't need full keys), and 2) do you see the failing requests in your dashboard request logs (match by client_user_id or IP)?

customer-jane: Active key ends with "-x4Qp9". Failing requests in our app show header value ending with "-K3m7s" (old key). Dashboard shows no entry for the new key for those users.

mia-support: That points to the client sending the old key (copy/paste or cache). Two likely culprits with PWAs: build artifact still bundling old env, or the service worker caching a older JS/worker script that holds the old key. Can you check the service worker registration and the cached worker version?

customer-jane: Confirmed — service worker script (sw.js) was last updated before rotation and contains the old key inside a const API_KEY = 'REDACTED-...-K3m7s'; our CI injects the key at build time. We pushed a new version but maybe not all clients updated.

mia-support: OK that's a repro. Quick remediation options: 1) invalidate the worker cache so clients fetch the new sw.js (set shorter cache-control / update SW version), or 2) rotate the key again and ensure build pipeline updates the deployed worker asset and triggers clients to update.

raj-sre: +1 on SW cache. We also see similar patterns where stale service workers pin secrets that were baked into the bundle. From infra logs I can check whether any edge cache is serving an older sw.js for that path — share the sw.js URL and I'll confirm.

customer-jane: sw.js URL: https://assets.customer-app.example.com/sw.js. We pushed new file at 09:05 UTC.

raj-sre: I queried the CDN: there are still edge nodes returning the 200 from a cached object version created 2026-03-16T08:50:02Z (older). CDN TTL was 24h. That explains why a subset of clients keep getting old worker. We'll purge the object now.

deploy-bot: purge request submitted for assets.customer-app.example.com/sw.js by raj-sre (purge-id: purge-9876).

customer-jane: Purge looks successful for most regions, thank you. We're still seeing a handful of 401s for older population — likely devices that haven't reloaded the SW in a while. Any advice for forcing update without user action?

mia-support: You can implement a short-lived fallback: issue a temporary key with same permissions and deploy it to a different header that isn't baked into SW (e.g., require server-side proxy to add x-api-key at runtime), but that's heavier. Simpler: bump SW version constant and set clients to check skipWaiting() + clients.claim() on install so they activate immediately on next navigation. For immediate relief, reissue keys and set the old key to expire in 1 hour so residual traffic fails faster (so they reauthenticate).

alex-eng: Adding: avoid baking secrets into any public JS or worker. Recommend storing keys server-side or using an ephemeral token service (exchange cookie-backed short token for API key). We'll prepare a short doc for the PWA team.

ops-doug: Flagging to infra: can we add a dashboard alert for CDN objects that contain the string pattern of API keys (regexp) to warn when keys are present in cached assets? Could help catch this before rotation.

raj-sre: Good idea — will prototype a low-risk scanner that checks cached objects for key-like patterns and emits a low-severity alert. ETA 2 weeks.

customer-jane: Thanks all — purge + rebuilding SW solved the bulk of the problem. We'll audit our build to remove secrets from the worker. Appreciate the quick help. :tada:
